surprises.description: Sales were $64.9 million, about 10% above the $58.98 million consensus and above even the preview’s $63 million bull case. The preview’s $60 million base case and roughly $60–61 million buy-side bar were also substantially exceeded.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 consolidated net sales rose 18.9% year-over-year to $64.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q1 FY27 Consensus | $58.98M”; the scenario analysis gave a “Base” revenue of “$60.0M” and “Bull” revenue of “$63.0M.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS of $0.27 far exceeded both the $0.09 consensus and the preview’s $0.11–$0.12 base case, and was above its $0.16–$0.18 bull range. Operating income also reached $5.1 million, or 7.9% of sales, indicating much stronger profitability than the preview’s modeled operating leverage implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating income increased over 400% to $5.1 million (7.9% of sales)”; “diluted EPS reached $0.27 versus $0.13.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS (GAAP) | Q1 FY27 Consensus | $0.09”; the preview’s base case was “$0.11–0.12” and bull case “$0.16–0.18.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 34.6%, well above the preview’s roughly 31.3% model. A 170-basis-point tariff refund was non-recurring, but excluding it leaves margin at about 32.9%, still above the modeled level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin expanded to 34.6% from 31.0%, though 170 basis points of the improvement came from a non-recurring IEEPA tariff refund that management cautioned may not continue.”

surprises.description: Backlog rose to $184.4 million, up $20 million sequentially, rather than declining modestly as the preview said would be tolerable. It also substantially exceeded the preview’s $170 million bull-case marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total backlog grew to $184.4 million, up $20 million (about 12% sequentially) from fiscal 2026 year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 is seasonally softer and Q4 likely pulled shipments forward, so a modest sequential decline is tolerable”; the bull case cited “backlog >$170M.”

surprises.description: PMT sales were $46.6 million excluding legacy healthcare, above the preview’s roughly $43 million base/whisper and near its $46 million bull-case estimate. The reported 23.1% growth excluding legacy healthcare is consistent with stronger-than-base semiconductor and RF/microwave demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PMT sales grew 19.7% (23.1% excluding legacy healthcare, to $46.6 million), driven by semiconductor wafer fab and RF/microwave products in SATCOM, radar, and defense markets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case estimated “PMT ~$43M”; its catalyst checklist called “~$43M” the whisper, while the bull case estimated “PMT ~$46M.”

surprises.description: GES sales rose 27.1%, about $2 million, and management now expects double-digit growth for all of FY2027. That is stronger near-term growth framing than the preview’s roughly $8 million quarterly base and its characterization of FY2027 as a pipeline-building year, with meaningful BESS revenue growth expected in FY2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GES sales rose 27.1% ($2.0 million) with growth mostly from wind products, and management expects double-digit GES growth for full-year FY2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case estimated “GES ~$8M” and described FY27 as a “pipeline-building” year, with “meaningful revenue growth expected in fiscal 2028.”

surprises.description: Operating cash flow was $5.9 million and cash rose to $36.9 million, above the $31.8 million cash balance cited in the preview. The preview did not set a cash-flow expectation, so this is an unanticipated improvement rather than a miss against a stated forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash operating activities generated $5.9 million versus $1.4 million a year earlier, boosting cash and equivalents to $36.9 million from $31.8 million, with the company remaining debt-free.”
